title: AI in your pocket
caption:
AI used to need a data centre. Now chips are built to run a 30B model on a phone 📱

Riya asks, Arjun explains:
1. The real wall: memory
2. Quantization: fewer bits per number
3. Mixture of experts: only wake who you need
4. Putting it together on a phone chip
5. Why it matters (and the catch)

Pause at the 2 quizzes and guess before the reveal 🧠

Facts: Google Gemma 4 docs, Liquid AI LFM2.5-24B-A2B blog, Qualcomm via TechCrunch (Sept 2026).

Next up: the "think harder" dial ⏱️

scenes.title: AI IN YOUR POCKET
scenes.subtitle: How a 30B model fits on a phone chip

lines.vo: Arjun, I read that a new phone chip can run a thirty billion parameter A.I. model. On a phone?
lines.cap: A 30 BILLION parameter AI... on a PHONE?

lines.vo: Yep. Qualcomm says its top Snapdragon chip can run one locally. No cloud. Let's see how that's even possible.
lines.cap: No cloud. Let's see HOW that's possible.

lines.vo: So what was stopping it before? Phones are pretty fast.
lines.cap: What was stopping it? Phones are FAST.

lines.vo: Speed isn't the wall. Memory is. A model is billions of numbers, and normally each one takes sixteen bits. That's two bytes.
lines.cap: The wall is MEMORY. Each number = 16 BITS.

lines.vo: Google's Gemma four E4B needs about eighteen gigabytes at sixteen bit. Eight bit halves that. Still too big for most phones.
lines.cap: Gemma 4 E4B: ~18 GB. Still TOO BIG.

scenes.label: QUIZ 1
scenes.question: Same model, 4 bits per number instead of 16. How much memory?

lines.vo: Okay, quiz time. Same model, but four bits per number instead of sixteen. How much memory?
lines.cap: QUIZ: 4 bits instead of 16. How much memory?

lines.vo: Pause and guess. Three, two, one.
lines.cap: Pause and GUESS. 3... 2... 1...

lines.vo: About four and a half gigabytes. A quarter of the bits, a quarter of the size.
lines.cap: About 4.5 GB. A QUARTER of the size.

lines.vo: That trick is called quantization. You store every number with fewer bits, like saving a photo with fewer colours.
lines.cap: QUANTIZATION: fewer bits, like fewer COLOURS.

lines.vo: But if you squash the numbers, doesn't the A.I. get dumber?
lines.cap: Doesn't the AI get DUMBER?

lines.vo: A little, if you just squash a finished model. So Google trains Gemma while simulating the low precision. That's called quantization aware training.
lines.cap: Train it WHILE simulating low precision: QAT.

lines.vo: The model learns to cope with rough numbers. Their mobile version of E4B gets down to about two and a half gigabytes.
lines.cap: Mobile E4B: about 2.5 GB.

lines.vo: And if you go even lower?
lines.cap: And even LOWER?

lines.vo: Then the picture really breaks. Squash too far and quality drops.
lines.cap: Too far and QUALITY drops.

lines.vo: Okay, but thirty billion is still huge. What's the second trick?
lines.cap: 30 billion is still HUGE. Trick number two?

lines.vo: Mixture of experts. Instead of one giant brain, the model is split into many smaller expert networks.
lines.cap: MIXTURE OF EXPERTS: many small expert networks.

lines.vo: For every word, a router wakes up just a few of them. The rest sit idle.
lines.cap: A ROUTER wakes just a FEW per word.

lines.vo: Liquid A.I.'s new model has twenty four billion parameters, but only two billion work on each word. It picks four of sixty four experts.
lines.cap: 24B total, only 2B ACTIVE. 4 of 64 experts.

lines.vo: On a MacBook with an M5 Max chip, Liquid says it runs at one hundred eighty four tokens a second.
lines.cap: 184 TOKENS a second on a laptop.

scenes.label: QUIZ 2
scenes.question: 24B total, 2B active. What does mixture of experts save?

lines.vo: Wait, so it saves memory too, right? Only two billion are working.
lines.cap: So it saves MEMORY too, right?

lines.vo: That's our second quiz. Memory, compute, or both? Three, two, one.
lines.cap: Memory, compute or BOTH? 3... 2... 1...

lines.vo: Compute. Every expert still has to sit in memory, ready to be picked. Google says the same about its own twenty six billion expert model.
lines.cap: COMPUTE. All experts still sit in MEMORY.

lines.vo: So how does it all fit on a phone?
lines.cap: So how does it all FIT?

lines.vo: Stack the tricks. Quantization shrinks the memory.
lines.cap: QUANTIZATION shrinks memory.

lines.vo: Mixture of experts means each word only needs a small slice of the work.
lines.cap: EXPERTS cut the work per word.

lines.vo: And new chips add more memory and dedicated A.I. hardware.
lines.cap: New CHIPS add memory and AI hardware.

lines.vo: Together, that's how Qualcomm can claim a thirty billion mixture of experts model on a phone.
lines.cap: That's how 30B on a PHONE becomes possible.

items.s: your data stays on the device
no server wait, no per-token bill
battery, heat, still behind cloud models

lines.vo: Why should I care if it runs on my phone?
lines.cap: Why should I CARE?

lines.vo: Privacy, for one. Your messages and photos never leave the device. And it works offline.
lines.cap: PRIVACY, and it works OFFLINE.

lines.vo: There's no waiting on a server, and no bill for every token.
lines.cap: No server wait. No per-token BILL.

lines.vo: There has to be a catch.
lines.cap: There has to be a CATCH.

lines.vo: Battery and heat. And the biggest cloud models are still smarter. So phones will handle the everyday stuff, and the cloud the heavy lifting.
lines.cap: BATTERY, heat, and the cloud is still SMARTER.

lines.vo: So, memory is the wall, fewer bits shrink it, experts cut the work, and the chips caught up.
lines.cap: MEMORY, BITS, EXPERTS, CHIPS.

lines.vo: Exactly. Next time, the think harder dial. Follow so you don't miss it.
lines.cap: Next: the THINK HARDER dial. FOLLOW!
